scope: Four activities selected for distinct current inferences, not a fixed practice count. Complete prompt/interface/hint/model/criteria are extracted from the actual final fragments. No annotation substitutes for learner content.

items.title: Repair the two process labels
items.sourcePurpose: Separate homologous segregation within one parent from fertilisation between parental gametes. Kinch slides17–23 supply the seed-generation method; slide22 conflates their roles. The full visible arrow table provides the representation to repair.
items.uniqueContribution: Students locate a mechanism error in an existing representation and explain separation versus joining. This is not another numerical F2 cross or a repeated parentage-classification exercise.
prerequisiteAnchors: current trial ch17-l02-worked before this task
items.protectedAnswerDisposition: Necessary segregation/fertilisation/F1–F2 concept overlap remains. This task does not reproduce the protected F1/F2 written prompt or the six-dominant-offspring required case. It changes the action to repairing two explicit process labels.
items.exemplarFunction: Chapter11 lesson02 Explain a diagram error: full flawed representation, guided causal repair, and feedback checking the location and consequence of the error.
items.essentialBeforeAttempt: Homologues and sister chromatids, one-allele gamete contribution, fertilisation restoring a pair, simple F2 combination model. The model disclosure adds comparison, not essential instruction.
items.progress: Optional and ungraded; native S.notes proposal; outside required progress.

items.title: Does reversing the parents reverse the result?
items.kind: independent parental-role claim evaluation, scaffolded near transfer
items.sourcePurpose: Retain the source RR×rr core while requiring an inference about reciprocal parent roles, each offspring seed's own genotype and the pollen recipient's phenotype.
items.uniqueContribution: The learner rejects a receiving-plant shortcut by tracing both contributions in reciprocal records. It uses the already worked genotype result and is not presented as a new mathematical cross or blind assessment.
prerequisiteAnchors: current trial ch17-l02-teaching-01 controlled crossing and seed transition
current trial ch17-l02-worked fertilisation and autosomal model
items.protectedAnswerDisposition: No exact required reciprocal-role response collision was found in the bounded native task review. The RR×rr all-Rr result is deliberately reused and disclosed. A prior RR×Rr candidate was rejected because it relabelled the protected lesson03 only-dominant-phenotype case.
items.exemplarFunction: Chapter11 lesson02 Compare two different failures: change the inference demanded by the task; state the full evidence and assess a proposed explanation. This does not copy the nervous-system story or its example count.
items.essentialBeforeAttempt: Explicit autosomal seed-own-genotype model and complete dominance, known reciprocal parental genotypes, gamete contributions and fertilisation. No parental-origin exception mechanism is required.
items.progress: Optional and ungraded; native S.notes proposal; outside required progress.

items.title: Change one parent and keep only the reasoning that still applies
items.sourcePurpose: Extend the source's distinct-gametes-before-grid method by changing the second tomato parent from RRTt to RRtt. Keep unchanged colour reasoning while recomputing the height contribution and grid size.
items.uniqueContribution: Diagnose which parts of a solved method survive a specific change. The new case has four distinct gametes versus one and a different height probability, so it does not reproduce the protected four-versus-two written response or one-eighth phenotype target.
prerequisiteAnchors: current trial ch17-l05-worked tomato application before this task
items.protectedAnswerDisposition: The new activity's four-by-one case and one-half short event are distinct from the protected written cases. The preceding worked tomato's four-by-two structural overlap remains unresolved; this activity does not cure that conflict. The feedback distinguishes unnecessary duplicated columns from the biologically invalid retention of an RT gamete from RRtt.
items.exemplarFunction: Chapter11 lesson02 diagram repair and failed-repair comparison; Chapter11 lesson06 worked quantitative model: preserve givens, justify each changed operation, check and interpret.
items.essentialBeforeAttempt: Both tomato allele mappings, parental gamete derivation, product probabilities, distinct-gamete grid sizing, genotype-to-phenotype grouping and the all-red conclusion are visible before the task.
items.progress: Optional and ungraded; native S.notes proposal; outside required progress.

items.title: Decide what the new offspring settles—and what it leaves open
items.sourcePurpose: Transfer the squash inverse inference to a new hypothetical V/L model where the observed offspring forces only one unknown parental allele, not both.
items.uniqueContribution: Distinguish possible from forced genotypes under partial evidence and identify a further informative observation. It tests the limit of applying the previous inference indiscriminately; it adds no posterior weighting or selected-record denominator.
prerequisiteAnchors: current trial ch17-l05-teaching-03 squash inverse reasoning before this task
items.protectedAnswerDisposition: No exact required full response collision was found in the bounded review. Possible/forced genotype reasoning deliberately builds on native04. The model uses different phenotypes/evidence and resolves only one parental blank; it does not re-answer the source squash double-recessive case.
items.exemplarFunction: Chapter11 lesson02 Compare two different failures: change what the evidence can establish, test an overextended explanation and explain the limit of a proposed conclusion.
items.essentialBeforeAttempt: Full phenotype mapping, visible parental record, one observed child, the meaning of genotype blanks, recessive contribution reasoning, and the finite-observation limitation from actual native04.
items.progress: Optional and ungraded; native S.notes proposal; outside required progress.
